focus.jnote: The Fed is behind us, but the AI trade just wobbled. The S&P 500 gained 0.28% to close at a record 7,743.98 Wednesday, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.27% to 26,549.85. The index edged higher after the Federal Reserve paused its tightening cycle in a split 10-2 vote without ruling out a December hike. Then the earnings landed: Alphabet shares dropped more than 10% in premarket trading after missing third-quarter expectations, mainly on weak revenue from its services unit, while Microsoft gained after beating forecasts on 48% Azure cloud growth. Dow futures slipped below the flatline, S&P futures slid ~0.2%, and Nasdaq-100 futures fell ~1%. Oil eased but stayed high: Brent fell ~1% to $114.2 and WTI slipped on US-Iran peace hopes, though Houthi attacks kept supply risk alive. The VIX closed Wednesday down 3.5% at 16.91 and ticked back up in futures. This is a live AI-earnings whipsaw with more mega-caps tonight — not a clean premium-selling backdrop.
focus.notdown: Of the boarded bullish names, the cleanest is CROX. Crocs beat revenue expectations with sales up 4.6% to $1.04 billion, and its next-quarter guidance of $1.03 billion came in ~4% above consensus. The stock jumped 19.3% to ~$142.82 in Thursday's premarket. AEP (A, bullish) is a textbook clean print — EPS of $2.23 beat by $0.19 on revenue of $6.83B, up 13.7% YoY — and it raised its long-term growth outlook. ORLY (A, bullish) beat and raised. All are bullish, but every one printed on near-zero relative volume (0.00–0.15x), so the moves lack participation confirmation. Watch-only on a RED day.
focus.notup: Two bearish Type A names boarded — CTSH and AXTA. Cognizant fell 8% premarket after reporting a 7% decline in third-quarter bookings and soft Q4 guidance, even though revenue rose 4.6% to $5.66 billion and adjusted EPS rose 7.2% to $1.49. Axalta's results fell short of Wall Street — adjusted EPS of 63 cents versus the 71-cent estimate, but the stock carries an AkzoNobel merger overhang. Selling bear calls into an AI-earnings whipsaw with the VIX ticking up invites a squeeze on any relief headline — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? P(≥1% gap) at ~38% is above the 35% trigger — that alone locks out GREEN — and composite ~59 is deep in WARM. On top of the math, Amazon, Intel, Caterpillar and Eli Lilly are all slated to report earnings today, with Apple also in the queue — fresh mega-cap gap catalysts inside any normal DTE, and the Alphabet reaction shows how violent these can be. Add a live oil tail and every boarded name printing on near-zero volume, and this is not a tape to underwrite new premium into. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past tonight's prints and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: Mega-cap earnings tonight — Amazon, Intel, Caterpillar and Eli Lilly all report today, with Apple also due. After Alphabet's ~10% drop, any guidance disappointment on AI capex or cloud is a double catalyst that can re-crack the whole index — keep every spread clear of its name's print.

The AI-capex narrative — markets are no longer rewarding companies simply for investing heavily in AI and increasingly demand evidence that spending generates sustainable profits. The Alphabet-vs-Microsoft split shows how violently single names can gap on this theme.
Oil & the 10-year — the 10-year rose ~6 bps to 5.05%, its biggest one-day rise in a month, while WTI holds ~$102 and Brent ~$115. A rate pop stacked on an oil tail keeps pressure on equities.

Middle East supply tail — Houthi attacks keep supply-disruption risks alive even as reported U.S.–Iran peace overtures ease some concern. A collapse in talks or a Hormuz incident is the week's biggest open-ended risk.

ECB (Thu) & BoJ (Fri) — a back-to-back central-bank gauntlet follows the Fed, able to whipsaw rates, the dollar and risk into the weekend. Plus every boarded name printed on near-zero relative volume — treat all seven as watch-only.
